Please answer this question with a number--which of the following best apply to the design in the study: 
        (1) totally fun first (i.e., Entertainment game reappropriated), 
        (2) mostly fun first (i.e., design workshop with disabled stakeholders),
        (3) both fun and utility first (i.e., design workshop with diverse stakeholders), 
        (4) mostly utility first (i.e., primary utilitarian mechanic designed first),
        (5) totally utility first (i.e., made by clinicians or specialists, fun incorporated later)
reasoning: The exergame FroggyBobby is explicitly designed to support motor rehabilitation and self-care activities for children with motor problems, using an iterative user-centered methodology with psychologist-teachers and an HCI expert, not primarily as an entertainment game. The primary focus is on gross and fine motor coordination exercises and therapeutic/assistive goals, with game elements layered on top, which aligns best with a mostly utility-first design where the utilitarian mechanic is primary and fun is incorporated to maintain engagement.

        (1) unstructured play (i.e., no rules, making art),
        (2) semi-structured play (i.e., playground activities),
        (3) flexible structure with rules (i.e., improv),
        (4) flexible game (i.e., board game with house rules),
        (5) game with rigid rules (i.e., video game)
reasoning: FroggyBobby is described as an exergame with defined levels, specific required movements (e.g., moving arms along a path from start to end buttons, catching flies one at a time), and Kinect-tracked actions, indicating a structured game with explicit rules rather than open or loosely structured play. This aligns best with a game with rigid rules.

Please answer this question with a number--which of the following best apply to the design in the study: 
        (1) entirely skill-based (i.e., trivia, sports),
        (2) mostly skill-based (i.e., mario kart),
        (3) equally skill and chance-based (i.e., catan),
        (4) mostly chance-based (i.e., Uno),
        (5) entirely chance-based (i.e., all dice)
reasoning: The exergame FroggyBobby requires players to perform specific gross and fine motor movements tracked by Kinect (arm swipes, presses, grips, fine pincer) to catch flies or manipulate objects. Outcomes depend on the accuracy of these motor skills rather than random elements; no chance-based mechanics (dice, random draws affecting success) are described. This makes the design entirely skill-based.

        (1) entirely solo (i.e., solitaire),
        (2) mostly solo (i.e., playing against AI in single-player StarCraft),
        (3) mix of solo and social affordances (i.e., animal crossing),
        (4) mostly social, but aspects are independent (i.e., house on hill haunt transition),

reasoning: FroggyBobby is described as an exergame where a child controls a frog avatar with their own arm and hand movements to catch flies and practice motor exercises. There is no mention of multiplayer features, other players, or social interaction; all gameplay and mini-games are framed as individual therapeutic practice, indicating an entirely solo design.

question:
Please answer this question with a number--which of the following best apply to the design in the study: 
        (1) entirely turn-based (i.e., tic tac toe),
        (2) follows a set of steps (i.e., viticulture's dynamic turn ordering),
        (3) turns are taken, but some actions can be taken at any time (i.e., pandemic),
        (4) most actions can be taken at any time, but there are some phases (i.e., PvP death reset timer),
        (5) entirely simultaneous (i.e., race)
reasoning: FroggyBobby is a single-player Kinect exergame where the child continuously moves their arms to control the frog’s tongue and catch flies. There is no mention of discrete turns, phases, or restricted timing of actions; instead, movement and catching flies appear to be continuous and real-time, fitting an essentially simultaneous-action design rather than turn-based or phased structures.

Please answer this question with a number--which of the following best apply to the design in the study: 
        (1) entirely synchronous (i.e., real time strategy game),
        (2) mostly synchronous with a few asynchronous affordances (i.e., league of legends),
        (3) equal mix of synchronous and asynchronous affordances (i.e., helldivers 2),
        (4) mostly asynchronous with few synchronous affordances (i.e. cookie clicker),
        (5) entirely asynchronous (i.e., chess by postage mail)
reasoning: FroggyBobby is an exergame where children control a frog in real time using Kinect-tracked arm and hand movements to catch flies and interact with on-screen targets. The gameplay described (moving arms to catch flies, pressing, gripping, fine pincer actions) is continuous, movement-based, and immediate-response, with no mention of turn-taking, delayed actions, or offline/asynchronous mechanics. This aligns with an entirely synchronous design.

This aligns with an entirely collaborative/solo-cooperative design rather than any competitive structure.
